page: Amazon Web Services m7a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the configuration includes 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a sustained base frequency of 3.7 GHz. The compute topology features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 support. Memory provisioning stands at 16.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core.

The instance contains no integrated GPUs and does not provide bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence depends on attached network-based Elastic Block Store volumes. Network capabilities include a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation, managed through the hardware-offloaded Nitro hypervisor. The absence of local scratch disks shifts IOPS capacity and storage throughput entirely to network storage parameters.

Benchmark testing highlights distinct performance characteristics across compute and memory subsystems. Single-core processing demonstrates top-tier capability, with stress-ng single-core reaching 3077.37 and Geekbench single-core recording 1936.0, both placing in the upper 25 percent. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing also showcase top-quartile execution speeds. In contrast, multi-core workloads, such as Clang compilation, PassMark CPU tests, and multi-threaded decompression, align with middle-tier averages across equivalent core allocations. A notable bottleneck appears in large-block uncached memory operations, where 256 MB sequential read and write speeds drop to the lower 25 percent, despite standard cached throughput at 585.94 GB/sec.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated-core execution model eliminates virtual thread contention, providing consistent performance per resource unit for multi-tenant deployments. The m7a.xlarge serves balanced production environments effectively, including application middleware, containerized microservices, static web serving, mid-range Redis caching nodes, and software build pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.7 GHz with one thread per core, paired with 16 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes for persistent storage, while providing a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 for accelerated compute operations. In benchmark evaluations, the m7a.xlarge demonstrates top-quartile single-core CPU throughput and strong bzip3 decompression, alongside average multi-core processing, static web serving, and Redis key-value throughput. However, large-block uncached memory operations fall into the lower performance quartile. The balanced resource configuration makes this instance well-suited for medium-scale web application serving, backend microservices, Redis caching tiers, Clang build pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting.
